newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond and PIBOR futures ended lower on Thursday as markets were unable to capitalise on mostly friendly U.S. data.

Prices were also hit at the end of the day by rumours of a new poll showing the left taking the lead in a parliamentary election set for May 25 with a final round June 1. The poll, by IPSOS for Le Point magazine, will be released at 1630 GMT.
Another factor weighing on the market was a wait-and-see attitude settling in among investors ahead of the May 20 policy-setting meeting at the U.S. Federal Reserve, analysts said.
Many analysts expect the Fed to raise rates next week even though U.S. price data was somewhat subdued this week. Producer prices fell and consumer prices rose 0.1 percent overall.
Analysts said the 0.3 percent rise of CPI excluding food and energy prices was slightly worrying, and in an uncertain market this could have weighed.
Markets are ready for a rate rise and are unlikely to suffer too much if the Fed acts. But real gains were unlikely unless the U.S. central bank held steady.
Consolidation hit Bunds, with the OAT/Bund spread unchanged at -14 points and traders said the market was bullish.
PIBOR suffered the most from the rumours about the upcoming poll, but dealers said this market, too, was fundamentally bullish.
"When we heard the rumour, everybody sold at the same time," one trader said.
The franc remained firm, trading at 3.3682 per mark late in the afteroon.
